import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

def run(inputs: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> dict[str, pd.DataFrame]:
    dim_price = inputs["dim_price"].copy()
    stg_price = inputs["stg_price"].copy()
    batch_control = inputs["batch_control"].copy()
    
    batch_date = batch_control["batch_date"].iloc[0]
    
    # Initialize the output with current dimension data
    result = dim_price.copy()
    
    # Process each product in stg_price
    stg_price = stg_price.sort_values(["product_id", "effective_date"]).reset_index(drop=True)
    
    for product_id in stg_price["product_id"].unique():
        stg_rows = stg_price[stg_price["product_id"] == product_id].sort_values("effective_date")
        
        for _, stg_row in stg_rows.iterrows():
            prod_id = stg_row["product_id"]
            new_price = stg_row["list_price"]
            eff_date = stg_row["effective_date"]
            
            # Find the tail version (latest eff_start_date) for this product
            prod_versions = result[result["product_id"] == prod_id]
            
            if len(prod_versions) > 0:
                tail = prod_versions.loc[prod_versions["eff_start_date"].idxmax()]
                tail_idx = tail.name
                
                # Check if price is unchanged
                if tail["list_price"] == new_price:
                    # Skip, no new version
                    continue
                else:
                    # Close the tail version
                    result.loc[tail_idx, "eff_end_date"] = eff_date
                    
                    # Insert new version
                    new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                        "product_id": [prod_id],
                        "list_price": [new_price],
                        "eff_start_date": [eff_date],
                        "eff_end_date": [pd.NaT],
                        "is_current": [0]  # Will be set after loop
                    })
                    result = pd.concat([result, new_row], ignore_index=True)
            else:
                # Product is new, insert first version
                new_row = pd.DataFrame({
                    "product_id": [prod_id],
                    "list_price": [new_price],
                    "eff_start_date": [eff_date],
                    "eff_end_date": [pd.NaT],
                    "is_current": [0]  # Will be set after loop
                })
                result = pd.concat([result, new_row], ignore_index=True)
    
    # Set is_current flag: 1 if version covers batch_date, else 0
    result["is_current"] = 0
    
    for idx, row in result.iterrows():
        start = row["eff_start_date"]
        end = row["eff_end_date"]
        
        # Version covers batch_date if: start <= batch_date < end
        # end is exclusive; if end is NaT, version is open (extends to infinity)
        covers_batch = start <= batch_date
        if pd.notna(end):
            covers_batch = covers_batch and (batch_date < end)
        
        result.loc[idx, "is_current"] = 1 if covers_batch else 0
    
    # Ensure correct data types
    result["product_id"] = result["product_id"].astype("int64")
    result["list_price"] = result["list_price"].astype("float64")
    result["eff_start_date"] = result["eff_start_date"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    result["eff_end_date"] = result["eff_end_date"].astype("datetime64[us]")
    result["is_current"] = result["is_current"].astype("int64")
    
    result = result.reset_index(drop=True)
    
    return {"dim_price_out": result}
